nodes.summary: Let $P : \mathbb{N} \times \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}$ and $t : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}$. If $t$ is a threshold function for $P$ and $c > 0$ is a real number, then $k \mapsto c \, t(k)$ is also a threshold function for $P$.
nodes.title: Positive multiples of threshold functions

nodes.summary: For $d \ge 0$ let $Q_d$ be the $d$-cube, the grid graph on $\{0, 1\}^d$, with cost $2$ on every edge, and let $t : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}$ be a threshold function, as $d \to \infty$, for the probability that a uniformly random configuration of $s$ pebbles on $Q_d$ is solvable. Write $n = 2^d$ and $\lg = \log_2$. Then for every real $\varepsilon > 0$, as $d \to \infty$, $n^{1-\varepsilon} = O(t(d))$ and…
nodes.title: Pebbling threshold bounds for the cubes (Czygrinow–Wagner, Alon)

nodes.summary: For every positive integer $n$, every sequence $g_1, \dots, g_n$ of $n$ elements of $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ has a nonempty zero-sum subsequence with cross number at most one: there is a nonempty set $S \subseteq \{1, \dots, n\}$ of indices with $\sum_{i \in S} g_i = 0$ and $\sum_{i \in S} 1/\operatorname{ord}(g_i) \le 1$, where $\operatorname{ord}(g_i)$ is the additive order of $g_i$. The theorem is due to Lemke…
nodes.title: Lemke–Kleitman theorem

nodes.summary: Let $\Gamma$ be a finite abelian group of order $|\Gamma|$. Every sequence $g_1, \dots, g_{|\Gamma|}$ of $|\Gamma|$ elements of $\Gamma$ has a nonempty zero-sum subsequence with cross number at most one: there is a nonempty set $S \subseteq \{1, \dots, |\Gamma|\}$ of indices with $\sum_{i \in S} g_i = 0$ and $\sum_{i \in S} 1/\operatorname{ord}(g_i) \le 1$, where $\operatorname{ord}(g_i)$ is the order of $g_i$.
nodes.title: Zero-sum subsequences of cross number at most one (Geroldinger; Elledge–Hurlbert)

nodes.summary: For every finite abelian group $\Gamma$, the probability that a uniformly random sequence of length $0$ in $\Gamma$ is good equals $0$: the empty sequence has no nonempty zero-sum subsequence, so it is not good.
nodes.title: Good-sequence probability at length zero

nodes.summary: Let $\Gamma$ be a finite abelian group and $t \ge 0$ an integer. A sequence $g_1, \dots, g_t$ in $\Gamma$ is good if some nonempty set $S \subseteq \{1, \dots, t\}$ of indices has $\sum_{i \in S} g_i = 0$ and $\sum_{i \in S} 1/\operatorname{ord}(g_i) \le 1$, where $\operatorname{ord}(g_i)$ is the order of $g_i$. The good-sequence probability of $\Gamma$ at length $t$ is the number of good sequences of length $t$ in…
nodes.title: Probability that a random sequence is good

nodes.summary: Let $d$ and $k$ be natural numbers, let $w_0, \dots, w_{d-1}$ be natural numbers, let $x, y \in \{0, \dots, k-1\}^d$, and let $i \in \{0, \dots, d-1\}$. If $x_i \ne y_i$ and $x_j = y_j$ for every $j \ne i$, then the grid cost of the pair $\{x, y\}$ with cost $w_j$ in coordinate $j$ is $w_i$.
nodes.title: Grid cost of a pair differing in one coordinate

nodes.summary: Let $d$ and $k$ be natural numbers and let $w_0, \dots, w_{d-1}$ be natural numbers. The grid cost with cost $w_i$ in coordinate $i$ assigns to each unordered pair $\{x, y\}$ of points of $\{0, \dots, k-1\}^d$ the sum of the $w_i$ over the coordinates $i$ with $x_i \ne y_i$. On an edge of the grid exactly one coordinate differs, so an edge in coordinate $i$ costs $w_i$.
nodes.title: Grid edge costs

nodes.summary: Let $d \ge 1$ and let $w_0, \dots, w_{d-1}$ be natural numbers with $w_i \ge 2$ for every $i$. For each $k$ give the grid $P_k^d$ on $\{0, \dots, k-1\}^d$ the cost $w_i$ on every edge in coordinate $i$, and let $t : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}$ be a threshold function, as $k \to \infty$, for the probability that a uniformly random configuration of $s$ pebbles on $P_k^d$ is solvable. Write $\lg = \log_2$ and
nodes.title: Bushaw–Kettle pebbling threshold for grids

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $d$ and $k$, the $d$-dimensional grid $P_k^d = \square_{i\lt d} P_k$ is the simple graph on $\{0, \dots, k-1\}^d$ in which $x$ and $y$ are adjacent when there is a coordinate $i$ with $x_j = y_j$ for all $j \ne i$ and $|x_i - y_i| = 1$. For $k = 2$ this is the $d$-cube $Q_d$.
nodes.title: Grid graph

nodes.summary: If $\Gamma$ is a finite abelian group with at most two elements, then its half-good threshold $P_{1/2}(\Gamma)$ equals $1$.
nodes.title: Half-good threshold of a group of order at most two

nodes.summary: Let $d \ge 0$, let $p_1, \dots, p_d$ be primes, not necessarily distinct, and for each $k$ let $\Gamma_k = \prod_{i=1}^d \mathbb{Z}/p_i^k\mathbb{Z}$, and let $P_{1/2}(\Gamma_k)$ be its half-good threshold. Write $\lg = \log_2$. Then there is a real constant $C$ such that for all sufficiently large $k$,
nodes.title: Threshold version of Geroldinger's theorem

nodes.summary: For a finite abelian group $\Gamma$, $P_{1/2}(\Gamma)$ is the least $t \ge 0$ such that a uniformly random sequence of $t$ elements of $\Gamma$ is good (has a nonempty zero-sum subsequence with cross number at most one) with probability at least $1/2$, that is, such that at least half of the $|\Gamma|^t$ sequences of length $t$ are good. If no such $t$ exists, $P_{1/2}(\Gamma)$ is defined to be $0$.
nodes.title: Half-good threshold

nodes.summary: Let $\Gamma$ be a finite abelian group, written additively, and let $g = (g_1, \dots, g_t)$ be a sequence of $t$ elements of $\Gamma$. The sequence $g$ is *good* if there is a nonempty set $S \subseteq \{1, \dots, t\}$ of indices with $\sum_{i \in S} g_i = 0$ whose cross number $\sum_{i \in S} 1/|g_i|$ is at most $1$, where $|g_i|$ is the order of $g_i$.
nodes.title: Good sequences in a finite abelian group

nodes.summary: Let $P : \mathbb{N} \times \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}$, where $P(k, s)$ is read as the probability of an event in the $k$-th space when $s$ random elements are chosen. A function $t : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}$ is a *threshold function* for $P$ if $t(k) > 0$ for all sufficiently large $k$ and, for every function $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, $P(k, f(k)) \to 1$ as $k \to \infty$ whenever $t = o(f)$, and…
nodes.title: Threshold functions

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph with natural-number edge costs $w$. Every pebbling configuration $C$ on $G$ with $C(r) \ge 1$ for every vertex $r$ is solvable with respect to $G$ and $w$.
nodes.title: Configurations covering every vertex are solvable

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph on a vertex set $V$ with natural-number edge costs $w$. A configuration $C : V \to \mathbb{N}$ of pebbles is *solvable* if for every target vertex $r$ there is a finite, possibly empty, sequence of pebbling steps on $G$ with costs $w$ leading from $C$ to a configuration with at least one pebble on $r$.
nodes.title: Solvable pebbling configurations

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph on a vertex set $V$, and let $w$ assign a natural-number cost $w(uv)$ to each unordered pair of vertices $\{u, v\}$. For configurations $C, C' : V \to \mathbb{N}$, there is a pebbling step from $C$ to $C'$ if there is an edge $uv$ of $G$ with $0 < w(uv) \le C(u)$ such that $C'$ is obtained from $C$ by removing $w(uv)$ pebbles from $u$ and adding one pebble to $v$.
nodes.title: Lagarias–Saks pebbling step

nodes.summary: For every simple graph $G$ on a finite vertex set with natural-number edge costs $w$ and every $t \ge 0$, the probability that a uniformly random configuration of $t$ pebbles on $G$ is solvable is at most $1$.
nodes.title: The solvability probability is at most one

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph on a finite vertex set $V$ with $n$ vertices, let $w$ assign a natural-number cost to each unordered pair of vertices, and let $t \ge 0$ be an integer. A configuration of $t$ pebbles is a function $C : V \to \mathbb{N}$ with $\sum_{v \in V} C(v) = t$. nodes.title: Probability that a random pebbling configuration is solvable

nodes.summary: Write $\lg = \log_2$. Let $t$ be a threshold function, in $k$, for the probability that a uniformly random sequence of $s$ elements of $\mathbb{Z}/35^k\mathbb{Z}$ is good. Then there is a real constant $C$ such that for all sufficiently large $k$,
nodes.title: Threshold for good sequences in $\mathbb{Z}/35^k\mathbb{Z}$

nodes.summary: Write $\lg = \log_2$. Let $t$ be a threshold function, in $d$, for the probability that a uniformly random sequence of $s$ elements of $\mathbb{Z}_2^d$ is good, and write $n = 2^d$. Then for every $\varepsilon > 0$, $t(d) = O\left(n / (\lg \lg n)^{1-\varepsilon}\right)$ as $d \to \infty$.
nodes.title: Threshold for good sequences in $\mathbb{Z}_2^d$

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
